questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose the Nederlands because the country has an influential role in the Western colonization history, which I wished to learn more about and heard that the University of Leiden provided great courses concerning this. I also chose the Nederlands since I like to do cultural things in the weekends, and I know Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Utrecht and den Haag are cities with many nice offers (yoga communities, capoeira workshops, dance classes, concerts, bouldering gyms ect.)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very much due to my activities besides studying and some friends I made outside university that my study abroad was amazing. Also, the lectures were really interesting (especially those from the "Global and Comparative Philosophy" program), but the social life on university was difficult for me to engage in, since I had elective courses, and all the courses I followed were part of a program, often all the students knew each other for 1 or 2 years ahead.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy with some help, I have emailed a lot back and forth and used MS-team to talk to my contact person at Leiden University. Not very easy without help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive too much help, when I was finally there. It was mostly before my arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used Facebook groups, and I sent around 50 messages and emails to different people, who had a room available. I was lucky to find a place for 4 months (so knew I was gonna look for a place for the last month of June, since I was there in total of 5 months), in a house with 5 other women at my age, they became friends and they had a cute cat. I chose to live in Amsterdam (I searched in Den Haag as well), it's much easier to find something there, and also I did not wish to live in Leiden since it's a smaller city with less cultural offers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked to live in Amsterdam, it is super easy (though a little expensive) to take the train (29 minutes), but you can buy NS-packages with 40% less ticket price off rush hours. Also, my courses were only Mondays (3 courses) and Wednesdays (3 courses as well) so I only had to go back and forth those 2 days. I think Amsterdam gave me a little more flexibility, though I quickly needed to find a good study place (liberaries, Volks hotel, Amsterdam University ect), as I was not too often at Leiden University to study.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's difficult to find a place, the same as in Copenhagen fx, so search some months in advance, I searched 3 months before leaving, and make sure to write a nice little application that you can copypaste and send around to as many as possible. Facebook groups are great; "Kamer Gezocht/Aangeboden in Amsterdam" fx.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find courses that I could register for, but with help from the Leiden staff I found a possible schedule.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Reading through the course catalogue, make a cup of tea and be ready to sit there some hours to make sure you choose the right ones that fit your wishes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was video chatting from Denmark before arrival with the staff at Leiden. Very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had 4 that I really wished, and 2 that was okay.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: On Wednesdays I had 3 courses back to back, so from 11 til 17, after that I was so tired. And the last course from 15-17 was the one course I struggled the most with. So I would not recommend doing that, I think I was too tired to concentrate properly and containing more new information. Then rather take a single class another day.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is higher, as you have 6 courses with 5 points each, In Denmark you often have 15-point courses so to get 30 points in a semester you normally have 2 courses. The professors acted like each course counted as 15-point courses, not just 5, so the workload was heavy, and I had to do resits for 2 exams in the end to have more time to prepare myself for exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more professor to student than at University of Copenhagen, I feel UCPH is good to engage students in dialogues and discussions, and group assignements, I did not have those forms expect from African philosophy (our professor was so nice, and very passionate with having everybody engaging in the discussions, in this class the vibration was so alive and different from the auditorium teacher to student experience) and to some degree in Jazz history, not too much interaction between teacher and students, but a lot of listening exercises. That was cool!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
World Philosophy: Africa - 5 ECTS
Jazz History - 5 ECTS
Medieval Philosophy - 5 ECTS
World Philosophy: Middle East - 5 ECTS
Islam in the Modern World - 5 ECTS
History of Political Philosophy - 5 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
World Philosophy: Africa - 5 ECTS
The professor was so passionate and sharp, he really inspired me. 
Also World Philosophy: Middle East - 5 ECTS, both of those were a part of the Global and Comparative Philosophy program (minor). Could have been interesting to follow the whole program, as a minor student at Leiden University.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation was more expensive that I thought it would be. But in weekends you can travel free if you buy the NS Flex Weekend Vrij for 30 euros a month, then I got to visit many other dutch cities than Amsterdam. Especially I liked to go to den Haag to the beach.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was more expensive that I thought it would be. But in weekends you can travel free if you buy the NS Flex Weekend Vrij for 30 euros a month, then I got to visit many other dutch cities than Amsterdam. Especially I liked to go to den Haag to the beach.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know, did not participate in activites at the host institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Dance, yoga, bouldering (especially the latter, there are some great bouldering gyms, and it is a great way to blow out some steam after a whole days studying).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to the dunes in Den Haag, and end at the beach to take a swim. Also Wageningen is a cool city with a lot of Climate change awareness and biodynamic communities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy, very international country, and very similar to Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: An international melting pot, I love meeting people from all around the world, my four closest friends I got were from four different corners of the world. Very grateful to learn from other cultures than my own, it makes me humble, openminded and reflective.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do something besides studying that you value
Find a good place and rhythm where you can study. I found a new methods that I had not used before at University of Copenhagen, 25 minutes intensive studying, 5 minutes break, and so forth for some hours before a longer break to have lunch.
Long walks to clear your mind.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the work load, and be ready to study more. 
Also Leiden University is more conservative than I know from UCPH.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned so so much, both academically and on a person level. I am very thankful (though it was tough!!) for the weekly essays I had to write in Medieval philosophy and World Philosophy: Middle East, meaning I wrote 20 essays (5 pages each) on 12 weeks but those essays really helped me to get a grip on the material of the courses. Also, I found my voice in writing, and the essay questions were really interesting, fx: "How can philosophy help us overcoem sorrow" based on Boethius' philosophical work.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My course History of Political Philosophy, the course had a huge work load and was very heavy on new academic terms I have never encountered before. But I have learned so much and studied so hard for this one to keep up.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
